title: Hopper FP8 rollout: adaptive profile chooser and calibration CI
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need an enablement path for FP8 on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2 variants) that minimizes accuracy regressions and is automated into our CI and rollout process. Recent experiments show model-specific stability differences: E4M3 gives the best perf on many models but occasionally produces outlier degradations for long sequences or small-batch inference. This ticket builds an adaptive profile chooser plus stability fixes and a calibration CI pipeline to gate PRs/releases.

Goals:
- Provide an automated calibration workflow that produces per-model preferred FP8 profile (E4M3 or E5M2) and confidence metrics.
- Implement runtime heuristics to choose or fallback between E4M3/E5M2 per-request with minimal latency overhead.
- Add stability fixes discovered during validation (clamping, per-layer outlier handling, deterministic rounding fallback).
- Add CI gating: nightly calibration runs, accuracy/regression checks against the golden eval set, and PR checks for calibration-affecting changes.

Non-goals:
- Full INT8 pipeline overhaul (covered separately).
- New model retraining.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration CI produces a per-model profile and a confidence score; PRs that change quantization-affecting code must run calibration CI and pass thresholds.
- End-to-end accuracy regression on the golden benchmark: mean token-level delta < 0.5% and 95th percentile < 1.2% compared to baseline FP16 for approved models.
- Canary rollout path: canary 5% traffic on dedicated Hopper pool with automated rollback if accuracy or latency SLOs breach.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- E4M3 vs E5M2 selection: choose E4M3 when calibration CI confidence > 0.85 and per-layer scale histograms show <0.5% clipped activations; otherwise prefer E5M2. This trades maximum perf for controlled risk.
- Runtime dynamic selection: keep profile in model metadata and allow per-request override via headers for debugging. Selection check is a single metadata lookup (O(1)) to avoid runtime penalty.
- Fallback policy: detect sustained error spikes (rolling window of 1k requests) to auto-switch to E5M2 or FP16. Avoid flapping by requiring 3 consecutive windows before a forced switch.
- Calibration dataset: use our curated golden prompts (see links) covering short/long sequences, code, math, and instruction-style prompts.

Implementation plan:
1) Calibration pipeline (CI): create a new CI job ci/calibration/ci_calib_pipeline.yml that runs calibration, produces per-layer histograms, computes confidence, and stores artifacts in GCS.
2) Calibration algorithm updates: implement outlier handling and clamping in runtime/quant/quant_profiles.py and calibration script to compute optimal E4M3/E5M2 thresholds.
3) Runtime: expose profile metadata and fallback heuristics in serving runtime, add lightweight metrics (profile_selected, fallback_triggered).
4) Validation harness: extend tests/quant/test_accuracy_suite.py to include nightly runs against golden eval set and to compute acceptance metrics.
5) Rollout: configure canary route in Dedicated autopilot and add rollback triggers in console-2025.12 rollout policy.

Manual testing checklist before canary:
- Run calibration CI for top-20 models (by usage) and compare to manual baselines.
- Validate that for edge-case prompts (long sequences) E5M2 is selected when appropriate.
- Stress test fallback with simulated packet loss and concurrency spikes.

Notes on stability fixes included in this ticket:
- Add clamp to per-channel scale calculation to avoid extreme scale values from rare activations.
- Deterministic rounding toggle to reduce non-deterministic output shifts during quantization transitions.
- Improve quantization warm-up in continuous batching to ensure KV-cache compatibility.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Q/FP8+Hopper+Adaptive+Chooser
- Golden eval dataset: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-GoldenEvalSet
- Calibration CI proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146

Ops / Rollout plan:
- Nightly calibration runs create candidate profiles; flagged ones with low confidence are quarantined for manual review.
- Canary for 72h at 5% traffic -> 25% -> full, with automated rollback if token-level deltas exceed thresholds or latency P99 increases >15%.

Open questions:
- Acceptance thresholds: we set conservative defaults above; PM/RE needs to confirm final thresholds.
- Should we expose profile choice to customers (opt-in) or hide behind platform control? Current plan: platform-controlled with route-level overrides for early partners.
